chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who does not pray the morning (Fajr) prayer until it lightens and the redness appears, and he has not performed the two rak'ahs of Fajr. Does he perform them or delay them? He said, 'He delays them.'

key_terms.الْغَدَاةَ: The morning (referring to the time of Fajr prayer)
key_terms.تَظْهَرُ الْحُمْرَةُ: The redness appears (referring to the red glow in the sky at sunrise/shuruq)
key_terms.تُسْفِرَ: It lightens (referring to the early dawn light)
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: The two rak'ahs of Fajr (referring to the recommended sunnah prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the two sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr if one misses them along with the obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the distinction is made between the missed obligatory Fajr prayer and its two sunnah rak'ahs, ruling that the sunnah should be delayed until after sunrise (shuruq) rather than performed immediately with the qada of the fard. This highlights the specific jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the timing of sunnah prayers relative to the prohibited times of prayer (awqat al-karaha). The ruling underscores the flexibility in compensating for missed voluntary acts while maintaining the integrity of the obligatory prayer's schedule.
